methodological_rigor.justification: Technical methods paper evaluating MRI radiomic phantom design and reproducibility. Phantom constructed with 3D-printed PLA objects (grid and egg-shaped) filled with test materials (water, vitamin D3 capsules, olive oil). Scanned 10 times per scanner at 4+ institutions on various MRI platforms (Philips 1.5T, GE 1.5T, Siemens 1.5T, ViewRay 0.35T). Radiomic features extracted using Pyradiomics in 3D Slicer (n=107 features per object). Statistical analysis: Coefficient of Variation (CV) calculated for reproducibility assessment. However, no formal hypothesis testing, no power calculation, limited sample size of phantom objects (n=5), no inter-rater reliability for feature extraction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical technical/methodological study (LoE 5): phantom-based reproducibility assessment. No patients, no clinical outcomes. Addresses important infrastructure question for multi-institutional radiomics trials regarding quality control and standardization but does not directly impact patient care. Foundational work supporting future clinical radiomic studies but distant from clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods clearly describe phantom design, materials (PLA with/without wood particles), dimensions, filling materials, and MRI acquisition protocols across institutions. Radiomic feature extraction methodology documented (Pyradiomics, 3D Slicer, 107 features). Results presented with heatmap visualization of CV across scanners/objects. However, no formal reporting standard (ASTM, ISO, NIST guidance not referenced); limited supplementary detail on imaging protocols (Appendix referenced but visibility limited); no data/code sharing plan stated; reproducibility of feature extraction not assessed.

novelty_literature.justification: Addresses recognized gap in radiomic standardization literature: prior work (Lee et al., Bush et al., Mayerhoefer et al.) used various phantoms with inconsistent results. Novel aspect: 3D-printed design with modular grid/egg-shaped objects and multi-vendor/multi-site testing. However, phantom-based quality control is established methodology; similar approaches in prior cited literature. Incremental improvement on phantom design but limited methodological novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Introduction clearly motivates need for MRI radiomic standardization in multi-institutional trials and reviews prior phantom approaches. Methods logically describe phantom design, materials, imaging protocols, and feature extraction. Results presented with CV analysis and heatmap summary. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings relative to prior work. However, some technical density; limited discussion of clinical implications or recommended quality standards for future studies.

key_strengths: Addresses critical unmet need: standardized quality control methodology for radiomic features across multiple MRI vendors/models in multi-institutional trials
Comprehensive multi-site evaluation: 4+ institutions, multiple scanner models (Philips, GE, Siemens, ViewRay), T1/T2/TrueFISP sequences with 10 scans per scanner
Well-designed phantom with modular objects: grid objects (varying sizes/materials) and egg-shaped objects (tissue surrogates) enabling assessment across shape/texture ranges
Clear demonstration of inter-scanner variability: GE scanner better reproducibility than others; ViewRay (0.35T) showed <10% median CV for TrueFISP; egg-shaped objects less reproducible than grids
key_concerns: Preclinical technical study (LoE 5): no clinical validation; findings on phantom may not translate directly to patient imaging
Small phantom sample size (n=5 objects): limited generalizability; test materials (vitamin D3, olive oil) may not represent actual tissue properties across cancer types
No formal hypothesis testing; descriptive CV analysis only; no statistical comparison of inter-scanner differences
Missing reproducibility validation: inter-observer agreement for radiomic feature extraction not assessed; manual segmentation variability not reported
Limited actionable guidance: study identifies reproducibility issues but does not propose solutions or set quality thresholds for clinical trial acceptance
No prospective validation: future studies needed to confirm whether phantom-based standardization improves predictive accuracy in patient radiomic models
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid preclinical infrastructure study addressing important standardization question for radiomic trials, but LoE 5 and lack of clinical validation limit impact. Appropriate for Tier 4 (technical development study). Accept as foundation for future multi-institutional radiomic quality control; recommend prospective validation in patient cohorts.
